requirements.title: One mode table exists and is referenced from every doc page that mentions modes.
All docs and design surfaces agree on the same mode labels.
Test asserts every product mode has a label, shortcut, runtime-surface policy, and docs anchor.
Legacy labels are rejected outside the archived-evidence allowlist.
No broken reference to the missing plan remains.
Historical plan files are clearly marked supporting/historical.
New readers see the current product status before historical context.
Devil-era paths appear only in the allowlist and audit-reports/.
A Kanban board can be generated without manually interpreting prose.
All Kanban cards carry the required fields, enforced by the validator.
`verify-kanban-backlog` exits non-zero on any structural issue and reports the offending card.
No current doc cites ENGINEERING_AUDIT.yaml, ENGINEERING_STATUS.md, audit-reports/, .hermes/, or releases/v8.0.0/ as if present.
meta.plan points at an existing file; meta.milestone reflects the earliest milestone with open tasks; streaming and remote-transport task statuses match the tree and ADR-0046.
legion-app compiles with and without the ai feature; the no-default-features check runs in legion-gates.yml; legion-sandbox (DAP C4 sandboxing) is unconditional.
Per-format validation logic exists once in scripts; dpkg Maintainer is asserted; publish parses all five VALIDATION-SUMMARY.toml files and fails on any non-passed status.

GP-1 s3 passes against rust-analyzer 1.97.1 (native diagnostics served only via pull); the session advertises textDocument.diagnostic, records diagnosticProvider, and pull reports route through the same ingestion path as pushed notifications; push-only servers still pass via fallback.
A dispatched 3-OS run is recorded with per-job outcomes; failures are diagnosed toward the four-consecutive-green promotion criteria.
Every SmallCode module the port draws from has an explicit port/adapt/reject row with a Legion destination; rejected authority surfaces are named.
The SmallCode MIT license text is preserved verbatim and every derived area is traceable to its source module.
Fixture corpora exist as data files with license headers and definite expected outcomes; no Rust tests are wired yet (Phase 2 scope).
CI proves at least one keystroke-to-app-authority path through desktop UI.
legion-ui remains projection-only.
Each representative workflow has at least one headless test driving it through the harness.
Evidence document exists and cites the exact SHA + command output it was generated from.
Tests prove forbidden panels are absent in Manual mode.
Every layout region has a projection and an integration test.
Every interactive surface can be reached and operated without a pointer.
Restart restores the layout; nothing AI-relevant is persisted.
The CI gate fails if egui::TextEdit is reintroduced into the code canvas.
Editor is usable via rendered desktop UI, not only API tests.
A second cursor can be created, typed at, and cleared; every cursor is painted.
Token styles follow the active grammar; LSP diagnostics appear in the gutter and problems panel.
Input-to-paint budget evidence is generated.
A key typed in the code canvas reaches the Vim parser and moves the real cursor or edits the real buffer; normal-mode keys are not also inserted as text.
Test exists in ignored form, then is un-ignored once streaming mode is implemented.
100MB file opens within budget, scrolls, and does not block typing.
Projection explicitly enumerates the three states and consumers branch on it.
Streaming mode is visible in the UI with a plain-language explanation.
100MB workload is in the standard perf-harness run, not a side script.
A mock server launch is proven through the product registry, not a test-only path.
rust-analyzer lifecycle is supervised and projected; restart/backoff behavior is testable.
In the Legion repo, a real Rust diagnostic appears and clears after fixing.
Each LSP feature is reachable from the editor and is covered by a test.
Rename across files is reviewable and reversible.
Incoming and outgoing calls for the symbol under the caret are listed in a reachable panel, and the three call-hierarchy intents are removed from the intent-reachability allowlist.
Manual mode can run `cargo test` in a terminal tab and capture exit status metadata.
Denied/untrusted terminal paths still fail closed.
Terminal panel renders, scrolls, accepts input, and respects resize events.
OSC sequences are parsed and exposed as metadata; cwd/exit-code are queryable.
Trusted terminal runs equivalently on Windows via ConPTY.
DAP state machine drives a real adapter lifecycle, not only fixtures.
Adapter binary resolution is policy-gated; untrusted workspaces cannot launch debug adapters.
User can set a breakpoint, run a Rust test/binary, hit it, inspect locals, and continue.
Test list refreshes from LSP runnables and cargo test discovery.
Agents see structured debug/test evidence; raw payloads stay in the secure boundary.
Search is fast enough for the Legion repo.
Replace never mutates files outside proposal review.
Every command exposed in the palette is reachable from a keybinding or command-id list.
Search is bounded for large fixtures.
GP-1: open Legion repo, edit, see diff, stage hunk, commit, and optionally push.
Hunk staging and commit work end-to-end through the UI.
Agent worktrees are visible in the SCM panel; manual worktrees are managed by the user.
Every network/auth operation shows its policy decision to the user.
Every mutation route is documented with its current activation state.
Trusted local proposals can apply safely.
Denied future surfaces remain visibly denied.
Flags are removed/narrowed only with a paired test that proves the new behavior.
A 5-file AI/agent proposal can be reviewed, partially accepted, applied, and undone.
Each hunk can be accepted, rejected, or edited in place within the review surface.
Evidence panel shows structured fields, not freeform text dumps.
Every review action is reachable from the keyboard.
Every apply/batch leaves a checkpoint that can be restored.
Restore is a product feature, not just a hidden batch rollback primitive.
Restore does not stomp manual edits that did not conflict with the apply.
Every checkpoint and restore is queryable from the audit ledger.
Each rule has a stable id and an enumerated test case.
Auto-approval is opt-in and cites deterministic rule IDs.
Medium/high-risk proposals pause and explain why.
Classifier output is advisory; policy + human still gate the apply.
Hosted provider call is impossible without explicit workspace consent.
Provider keys are never written to a tracked config file.
Capabilities are queryable per provider and gated at activation time.
Recorded smoke tests run in offline CI; live smoke tests are gated by credential availability.
Manifest is a structured DTO, not a freeform prompt.
User can answer 'what left my machine?' before each AI run.
The bytes sent equal the manifest minus redacted items, with no other delta.
User can answer 'what left my machine?' after each AI run.
Assist mode is useful without granting direct mutation authority.
Each rail command is a tracked capability with a test.
Each streamed code block is rendered as an apply-as-proposal affordance.
Telemetry is metadata-only by default and is opt-in for richer fields.
GP-2 works on a real repo: explain -> refactor -> review manifest -> apply -> undo.
Each inline hunk is applied through the same proposal pipeline as multi-file proposals.
Undo restores the prior buffer state and a checkpoint entry exists for the apply.
Native agent can complete a scoped test-add task with audited tool calls.
Every tool call has a paired audit row with the same causality id.
Invalid tool calls are reported back to the model with structured errors.
Tool output is bounded; secrets and large blobs are redacted before reaching the model.
Every vector in the frozen SmallCode corpus is either recovered exactly or safely rejected; unrepairable inputs never yield a fabricated call; recovery never panics on truncated or adversarial input.

A malformed tool call cannot be dispatched (no input field exists on the variant); the loop reports the diagnostic back, counts it against the retry budget, and audits it as malformed_tool_arguments; transport-shape failures remain hard provider errors.

edit-as-proposal accepts an old_str/new_str fragment resolved against file content by exact unique match; zero or multiple matches are refused with a diagnostic naming the nearest line; whitespace and line-ending drift do not match; refusals are retryable within the run; the file on disk is never written.
Attempts to write outside scope or exfiltrate without permission fail closed and audit.
Worker writes are always inside a disposable scope; main workspace is never the direct target.
Each escape attempt fixture fails closed and is logged in the audit ledger.
User can see which sandbox is active and any platform-specific caveats.
Scope is a structured DTO; forbidden paths are enforced at tool-call time.
GP-3 works on Legion itself: scoped task -> worker -> evidence -> review -> apply.
Cancelled workers stop accepting tool calls and reap their worktree + sandbox.
Each state has an explicit UI affordance and a recovery test.
Workflow never starts from opaque instruction text; user can edit the plan first.
Each plan revision has an audit row and a diffable representation.
Approved plan produces a DAG with stable node ids; rejected plans do not produce a DAG.
Coordinator dispatches tasks to real workers; mock workers are out of the product path.
3-task DAG with one dependency runs with two parallel workers.
A conflict scenario pauses the workflow and surfaces a human-resolution affordance.
Merge-readiness report cites verification evidence per branch/task.
Board columns are driven by coordinator state, not by hand-edited state.
Each field is sourced from a structured coordinator projection, not a freeform string.
Each tag is enumerated and the stream renderer handles each one explicitly.
GP-4 works end-to-end through the app-owned workflow command-center projection, with desktop-rendered command-center rows consuming that projection.
A fresh ADR exists and the dependency policy reflects the choice.
External agent completes a scoped task without bypassing Legion policy.
Every external edit becomes a Legion proposal; every external log becomes an evidence row.
A Canvas control on the activity rail switches the centre; every open file is a card carrying its own text; a card can be dragged and two cards connected; the arrangement survives a restart.
Edges are the person's own claim, kept in their own type, so a derived import or call graph can be added later without reinterpreting them.
Dependency policy admits the chosen runtime and the ADR explains the choice.
WIT files compile and generate host bindings.
A fixture .wasm plugin loads, runs, and cannot escape permissions.
Each hostile fixture is contained and the audit row records the attempt.
User can install a safe bundled grammar/theme extension through product UI.
Each install prompts the user with a structured permission list.
A tampered artifact is refused before any code runs.
VSIX metadata is reported but never executed; no Node runtime is required.
Signer config exists in operator docs; no signing secret is committed.
Release descriptors carry real signer/verifier status or an explicit unsigned-beta status.
Fresh-VM install evidence is archived and cited from the readiness ledger.
If unsigned-beta is shipped, the policy is documented in operator docs and readiness ledger.

Apple Developer, Azure Trusted Signing, Linux signing keypair, update-feed host, cloud Mac, and live-eval API keys each have a checklist row, an EXT-* mapping, and an owner action; key inventory and escrow/rotation policy are recorded.
Strategy and manifest format are documented in an ADR and reflected in the pipeline config.
Each channel produces its own descriptor with no cross-channel leakage.

Update/rollback validated deterministically via the update-drill (19th standing gate). Note: the v0.1 plan referenced 'GP-5 update and rollback works' — that wording is superseded by the v0.2 rebaseline; the update-drill gate replaces the stale GP-5 reference. Binary swap/installer execution/restart remain out of scope (ADR-0042 D5).
Crash reporting is opt-in; the choice is stored in the audit ledger.

Induced crash produces symbolicated report only when consented. CAVEAT: native-fault minidump capture (crash-handler/minidumper crates) is explicitly deferred (D7); only Rust panic capture via std::panic::set_hook is implemented in v1. Induced panic via catch_unwind produces a consented crash bundle with panic.txt and summary.toml.
Default export is metadata-only; raw-data export is a separate, opt-in action.
xtask perf-harness enforces product workloads, not only synthetic stand-ins.
Perf-harness runs on all three OSes and archives the reports.
Each CI run archives a trend entry and the strict flag fails the build on regression.
Accessibility evidence is product-level, not just projection-level.
Each accessibility setting is exercisable through a test or a recorded walkthrough.
Each platform/OS combination has a recorded parity report.
Agent/product changes have measurable eval regression gates.
Each hostile fixture is scored and any successful exfiltration is a hard fail.
CI always runs recorded mode; live mode is opt-in and scheduled.

Bench scoring executes real fixture tasks (not synthetic budget arithmetic); the corpus spans >=15 tasks across >=3 fixture repos with a held-out subset; the raw (ungoverned) baseline for the reference local model is recorded with a task-set hash under plans/evidence/production/BENCH/baseline-raw-v1.md.
Security model matches the actual sandbox behavior, including documented Windows caveats.
Each secret-detection rule has a fixture and a test.
Org policy pack enforces a restrictive enterprise profile end-to-end.
An external audit/pen test is scheduled and its report is archived before any strong enterprise claim.
A fresh ADR exists and links the chosen CRDT/operation layer to the existing collaboration substrate.
Reconnect and offline behaviors are recorded as evidence.
Every Cloud Lane upload is paired with a visible egress manifest and is cancellable mid-flight.
Each surface has its own ADR, policy, tests, and product evidence before readiness status changes.
End-to-end consented trace -> adapter -> eval comparison is reproducible.
Raw trace storage is opt-in and redaction is enforced at the boundary.
Adapter training is reproducible and the comparison vs Legion-Bench baseline is archived.
